subject.title: Discord account-to-agent routing falls back to default agent instead of matching by account name

question: Should Discord add a guarded same-name accountId-to-agent fallback after explicit route bindings miss, or should explicit bindings remain the only supported routing contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but changing fallback behavior affects session ownership, model/provider context, and permission boundaries, and repository policy treats fallback semantics as product and security-sensitive.

options.title: Approve guarded fallback
options.body: Route non-default Discord accountIds to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with diagnostics, docs, regression tests, and live Discord proof.

options.title: Keep explicit bindings only
options.body: Leave runtime routing unchanged and add docs, doctor, or status warnings for named Discord accounts that look intended to bind to same-named agents.

options.title: Use the fork PR as source material
options.body: Review the external PR's approach only after resolving conflicts, confirming the contract, and adding the missing upgrade/security proof.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded fallback
recommendation.body: Route non-default Discord accountIds to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with diagnostics, docs, regression tests, and live Discord proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest routing ownership signal and authored the original multi-agent routing surface.
